correctness.rationale: For all r>=3 and u>=4, zero-sum distance-power quadratic form equals (q-1)Σpart-sums²-qΣvertex-weights². The sharp partwise Cauchy reduction gives q≤1/(1-μ). The 2×2 generalized eigenvalue has characteristic polynomial rvμ²-((r-1)u+2v)μ+u+r−2; its smaller root is μ. The other eigen exceeds 2/r via an explicit vector, and F(2/r,v)=(r−2)(1−u/r); implicit differentiation gives ∂μ/∂v=μ(rμ−2)/√Δ. Thus the ordering and equality locus hold for every admissible split. Endpoint inclusion and beyond-endpoint failure are witnessed by partwise-constant vectors. Reproducible checker: 1308 residual cases, 1080 balance comparisons, 133 full-matrix eigenvalue cases, 6 exact rational examples, none substituted for infinite proof.

value.rationale: A natural fixed graph-order/part-budget Hilbert snowflake threshold problem has a striking strict reversal of balanced-vs-extreme optimal profiles precisely at u=r, with all distinct profiles tied on the equality line. It yields a complete classification for the two-heavy-part family and a simple exact root formula, not an arbitrary chosen numerical slice or a textbook restatement. It does not claim a larger all-part multipartite classification.
